svg.title: Predictive Patch Scheduler risk-to-schedule map
svg.desc: A vulnerability record from manual entry, CSV or a sample generator is scored two ways in parallel: a deterministic rule computes a risk score and priority from CVSS, exploit availability and system criticality, and a Random Forest plus Gradient Boosting model predicts a risk score and priority from seven features; the models are trained on synthetic data whose labels come from the same rule formula, so the two paths largely agree. Both feed a priority-only schedule-time function, results are stored in SQLite with status always pending, and analytics, real-time alerts and the pending-patch view read from the database. No patch is ever applied.

VERIFIED LIMITS · FOUND IN CODE, NOT STATED IN THE README
At inference, LabelEncoder orders categories alphabetically (high, low, medium),
but training coded them high, medium, low — so “medium” and “low” are swapped.
No patch is ever applied. status stays “pending”; nothing is deployed, updated or
marked complete. Auth libs (jose, passlib, bcrypt) are listed but never imported.
